"""Unit tests for the JSON-file backed ``notes`` storage module.

Every test points the storage functions at a file inside ``tmp_path`` (either
directly through the ``path`` argument or by monkeypatching the working
directory), so the real ``notes.json`` next to the source is never read or
written.  Standard library plus pytest only.
"""

import json
import pathlib

import pytest

import notes


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# helpers / fixtures
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def read_json(path):
    """Parse *path* as JSON, failing loudly if it is not valid JSON."""
    text = pathlib.Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    return json.loads(text)


def texts(listed):
    """Return just the note bodies, which is what ordering assertions need."""
    return [note["text"] for note in listed]


@pytest.fixture
def store(tmp_path):
    """An isolated notes file path that does not exist yet."""
    return tmp_path / "data" / "notes.json"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# add_note + list_notes
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_add_then_list_returns_the_note(store):
    note = notes.add_note("buy milk", path=str(store))

    assert isinstance(note, dict)
    assert note["text"] == "buy milk"
    assert isinstance(note["created"], str) and note["created"]

    assert notes.list_notes(path=str(store)) == [note]


def test_add_multiple_notes_preserves_insertion_order(store):
    bodies = ["first", "second", "third"]
    returned = [notes.add_note(text, path=str(store)) for text in bodies]

    listed = notes.list_notes(path=str(store))
    assert texts(listed) == bodies
    assert listed == returned  # newest last, exactly as stored


def test_add_note_creates_missing_parent_directories(store):
    assert not store.parent.exists()

    notes.add_note("nested", path=str(store))

    assert store.is_file()


def test_list_notes_on_missing_file_returns_empty_list(tmp_path):
    missing = tmp_path / "does-not-exist.json"

    result = notes.list_notes(path=str(missing))

    assert result == []
    assert not missing.exists(), "listing must not create the file"


def test_list_notes_does_not_expose_internal_state(store):
    notes.add_note("a", path=str(store))

    listed = notes.list_notes(path=str(store))
    listed[0]["text"] = "tampered"
    listed.append({"text": "injected", "created": "x"})

    assert texts(notes.list_notes(path=str(store))) == ["a"]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# delete_note: happy paths
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_delete_removes_correct_entry_and_renumbers(store):
    for text in ("a", "b", "c"):
        notes.add_note(text, path=str(store))

    removed = notes.delete_note(2, path=str(store))

    assert removed["text"] == "b"
    remaining = notes.list_notes(path=str(store))
    assert texts(remaining) == ["a", "c"]
    # indexes are 1-based and renumber after a delete
    assert notes.delete_note(2, path=str(store))["text"] == "c"
    assert texts(notes.list_notes(path=str(store))) == ["a"]


def test_delete_first_and_last_entry(store):
    for text in ("a", "b", "c"):
        notes.add_note(text, path=str(store))

    assert notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store))["text"] == "a"
    assert notes.delete_note(2, path=str(store))["text"] == "c"  # was index 3
    assert texts(notes.list_notes(path=str(store))) == ["b"]


def test_delete_only_note_leaves_an_empty_json_array(store):
    note = notes.add_note("only", path=str(store))

    assert notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store)) == note

    assert read_json(store) == []
    assert notes.list_notes(path=str(store)) == []


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# delete_note: error paths
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_index", [0, -1, -3, 4, 99])
def test_delete_with_invalid_index_raises_value_error(store, bad_index):
    for text in ("a", "b", "c"):
        notes.add_note(text, path=str(store))

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        notes.delete_note(bad_index, path=str(store))

    # the failed delete left the store untouched
    assert texts(notes.list_notes(path=str(store))) == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert texts(read_json(store)) == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_delete_from_missing_file_raises_value_error(tmp_path):
    missing = tmp_path / "nothing-here.json"

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        notes.delete_note(1, path=str(missing))

    assert not missing.exists()


def test_delete_from_empty_store_raises_value_error(store):
    notes.add_note("temp", path=str(store))
    notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store))

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store))


def test_delete_rejects_non_integer_index(store):
    notes.add_note("a", path=str(store))

    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        notes.delete_note("1", path=str(store))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# on-disk representation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_file_holds_valid_json_after_each_operation(store):
    first = notes.add_note("first", path=str(store))
    raw_text = store.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert json.loads(raw_text) == [first]
    assert raw_text.endswith("\n")

    second = notes.add_note("second", path=str(store))
    assert read_json(store) == [first, second]

    # listing is a pure read: content is unchanged afterwards
    before_list = store.read_bytes()
    notes.list_notes(path=str(store))
    assert store.read_bytes() == before_list

    removed = notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store))
    assert removed == first
    assert read_json(store) == [second]


def test_written_file_is_a_json_array_of_objects(store):
    notes.add_note("checked", path=str(store))

    data = read_json(store)

    assert isinstance(data, list)
    assert len(data) == 1
    assert isinstance(data[0], dict)
    assert set(data[0]) == {"text", "created"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# default path is only ever used inside a tmp cwd
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_default_path_targets_the_current_directory(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    note = notes.add_note("default path works")

    assert (tmp_path / notes.DEFAULT_PATH).is_file()
    assert read_json(tmp_path / "notes.json") == [note]
    assert notes.list_notes() == [note]
    assert notes.delete_note(1) == note
    assert read_json(tmp_path / "notes.json") == []


def test_module_uses_only_standard_library():
    source = pathlib.Path(notes.__file__).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    imported = {
        line.split()[1].split(".")[0]
        for line in source.splitlines()
        if line.startswith(("import ", "from "))
    }
    assert imported <= {"json", "os", "datetime", "sys", "argparse", "typing"}
    assert "requests" not in imported

"""Tiny JSON-file backed notes storage.

Standard library only. No CLI code lives here; import the functions instead:

    import notes
    notes.add_note("buy milk")
    notes.list_notes()
    notes.delete_note(1)

Storage format: a JSON array of objects, newest last, e.g.

    [{"text": "buy milk", "created": "2024-05-01T12:00:00"}]
"""

import json
import os
from datetime import datetime

__all__ = ["add_note", "list_notes", "delete_note"]

DEFAULT_PATH = "notes.json"


def _load(path):
    """Return the notes list stored at *path* ([] when the file is missing)."""
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            raw = fh.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []

    if not raw.strip():
        # An empty file is treated like an empty notes list.
        return []

    data = json.loads(raw)
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        raise ValueError(
            "notes file %r must contain a JSON array, found %s"
            % (path, type(data).__name__)
        )

    notes = []
    for entry in data:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                "notes file %r must contain JSON objects, found %s"
                % (path, type(entry).__name__)
            )
        notes.append(entry)
    return notes


def _save(path, notes):
    """Write *notes* to *path* as a JSON array, creating directories as needed."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    if directory:
        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(notes, fh, indent=2)
        fh.write("\n")


def add_note(text, path=DEFAULT_PATH):
    """Append a note with *text* to the store and return the stored dict."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError("text must be a str, got %s" % type(text).__name__)

    notes = _load(path)
    note = {"text": text, "created": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    notes.append(note)
    _save(path, notes)
    return dict(note)


def list_notes(path=DEFAULT_PATH):
    """Return all notes as a list of dicts; [] when the file does not exist."""
    return [dict(note) for note in _load(path)]


def delete_note(index, path=DEFAULT_PATH):
    """Delete the 1-based note at *index* and return the removed dict.

    Raises ValueError for non-positive or out-of-range indexes (including
    when the file does not exist, since then nothing is in range).
    """
    if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
        raise TypeError("index must be an int, got %s" % type(index).__name__)

    notes = _load(path)
    if index < 1 or index > len(notes):
        raise ValueError(
            "index %d is out of range (file holds %d note(s))" % (index, len(notes))
        )

    removed = notes.pop(index - 1)
    _save(path, notes)
    return dict(removed)

"""Unit tests for the JSON-file backed ``notes`` storage module.

Every test points the storage functions at a file inside ``tmp_path`` (either
directly through the ``path`` argument or by monkeypatching the working
directory), so the real ``notes.json`` next to the source is never read or
written.  Standard library plus pytest only.
"""

import json
import os
import pathlib

import pytest

import notes


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# helpers / fixtures
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def read_json(path):
    """Parse *path* as JSON, failing loudly if it is not valid JSON."""
    text = pathlib.Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    return json.loads(text)


def texts(listed):
    """Return just the note bodies, which is what ordering assertions need."""
    return [note["text"] for note in listed]


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def guard_real_notes_file():
    """Fail if a test ever touches ``./notes.json`` in the workspace root."""
    real = pathlib.Path.cwd() / notes.DEFAULT_PATH
    before = real.read_bytes() if real.is_file() else None

    yield

    after = real.read_bytes() if real.is_file() else None
    assert after == before, "test read/wrote the working-directory notes.json"


@pytest.fixture
def store(tmp_path):
    """An isolated notes file path that does not exist yet."""
    return tmp_path / "data" / "notes.json"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# add_note + list_notes
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_add_then_list_returns_the_note(store):
    note = notes.add_note("buy milk", path=str(store))

    assert isinstance(note, dict)
    assert note["text"] == "buy milk"
    assert isinstance(note["created"], str) and note["created"]

    assert notes.list_notes(path=str(store)) == [note]


def test_add_multiple_notes_preserves_insertion_order(store):
    bodies = ["first", "second", "third"]
    returned = [notes.add_note(text, path=str(store)) for text in bodies]

    listed = notes.list_notes(path=str(store))
    assert texts(listed) == bodies
    assert listed == returned  # newest last, exactly as stored


def test_add_note_creates_missing_parent_directories(store):
    assert not store.parent.exists()

    notes.add_note("nested", path=str(store))

    assert store.is_file()


def test_list_notes_on_missing_file_returns_empty_list(tmp_path):
    missing = tmp_path / "does-not-exist.json"

    result = notes.list_notes(path=str(missing))

    assert result == []
    assert not missing.exists(), "listing must not create the file"


def test_list_notes_does_not_expose_internal_state(store):
    notes.add_note("a", path=str(store))

    listed = notes.list_notes(path=str(store))
    listed[0]["text"] = "tampered"
    listed.append({"text": "injected", "created": "x"})

    assert texts(notes.list_notes(path=str(store))) == ["a"]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# delete_note: happy paths
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_delete_removes_correct_entry_and_renumbers(store):
    for text in ("a", "b", "c"):
        notes.add_note(text, path=str(store))

    removed = notes.delete_note(2, path=str(store))

    assert removed["text"] == "b"
    remaining = notes.list_notes(path=str(store))
    assert texts(remaining) == ["a", "c"]
    # indexes are 1-based and renumber after a delete
    assert notes.delete_note(2, path=str(store))["text"] == "c"
    assert texts(notes.list_notes(path=str(store))) == ["a"]


def test_delete_first_and_last_entry(store):
    for text in ("a", "b", "c"):
        notes.add_note(text, path=str(store))

    assert notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store))["text"] == "a"
    assert notes.delete_note(2, path=str(store))["text"] == "c"  # was index 3
    assert texts(notes.list_notes(path=str(store))) == ["b"]


def test_delete_only_note_leaves_an_empty_json_array(store):
    note = notes.add_note("only", path=str(store))

    assert notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store)) == note

    assert read_json(store) == []
    assert notes.list_notes(path=str(store)) == []


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# delete_note: error paths
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_index", [0, -1, -3, 4, 99])
def test_delete_with_invalid_index_raises_value_error(store, bad_index):
    for text in ("a", "b", "c"):
        notes.add_note(text, path=str(store))

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        notes.delete_note(bad_index, path=str(store))

    # the failed delete left the store untouched
    assert texts(notes.list_notes(path=str(store))) == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert texts(read_json(store)) == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_delete_from_missing_file_raises_value_error(tmp_path):
    missing = tmp_path / "nothing-here.json"

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        notes.delete_note(1, path=str(missing))

    assert not missing.exists()


def test_delete_from_empty_store_raises_value_error(store):
    notes.add_note("temp", path=str(store))
    notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store))

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store))


def test_delete_rejects_non_integer_index(store):
    notes.add_note("a", path=str(store))

    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        notes.delete_note("1", path=str(store))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# on-disk representation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_file_holds_valid_json_after_each_operation(store):
    first = notes.add_note("first", path=str(store))
    raw_text = store.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert json.loads(raw_text) == [first]
    assert raw_text.endswith("\n")

    second = notes.add_note("second", path=str(store))
    assert read_json(store) == [first, second]

    # listing is a pure read: content is unchanged afterwards
    before_list = store.read_bytes()
    notes.list_notes(path=str(store))
    assert store.read_bytes() == before_list

    removed = notes.delete_note(1, path=str(store))
    assert removed == first
    assert read_json(store) == [second]


def test_written_file_is_a_json_array_of_objects(store):
    notes.add_note("checked", path=str(store))

    data = read_json(store)

    assert isinstance(data, list)
    assert len(data) == 1
    assert isinstance(data[0], dict)
    assert set(data[0]) == {"text", "created"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# default path is only used when a test explicitly redirects the cwd
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_default_path_targets_the_current_directory(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    note = notes.add_note("default path works")

    assert (tmp_path / notes.DEFAULT_PATH).is_file()
    assert read_json(tmp_path / "notes.json") == [note]
    assert notes.list_notes() == [note]
    assert notes.delete_note(1) == note
    assert read_json(tmp_path / "notes.json") == []


def test_module_uses_only_standard_library():
    source = pathlib.Path(notes.__file__).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    imported = {
        line.split()[1].split(".")[0]
        for line in source.splitlines()
        if line.startswith(("import ", "from "))
    }
    assert imported <= {"json", "os", "datetime", "sys", "argparse", "typing"}
    assert "requests" not in imported and "network" not in source.lower()

"""Make the project root importable so tests can ``import notes``.

pytest with the default ``prepend`` import mode only adds the directory of the
test file (``tests/``) to ``sys.path``, so the module under test in the project
root would not be importable when pytest is launched as a plain console
script.  Adding the root here keeps ``pytest tests/test_notes.py`` working
regardless of how it is invoked.
"""

import os
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
if ROOT not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

"""Shared pytest setup for the notes storage tests.

* Puts the project root on ``sys.path`` so ``import notes`` works no matter how
  pytest is launched (``pytest tests/...`` from a console script does not add
  the root directory by default).
* Provides an autouse guard that fails any test which reads or writes the real
  ``./notes.json`` in the project root.  Tests must use ``tmp_path`` instead.

Standard library plus pytest only.
"""

import os
import pathlib
import sys

import pytest

import notes

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
if ROOT not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def guard_real_notes_file():
    """Fail if a test touches the project-root ``notes.json``.

    An absolute path is captured before the test runs, so a test that
    ``monkeypatch.chdir``s into ``tmp_path`` is still checked against the real
    project directory.
    """
    real = pathlib.Path(ROOT) / notes.DEFAULT_PATH
    before = real.read_bytes() if real.is_file() else None

    yield

    after = real.read_bytes() if real.is_file() else None
    assert after == before, (
        "test touched the project-root notes.json; pass an isolated "
        "tmp_path (or chdir into tmp_path) instead"
    )
